name: Munmorah-Tuggerah Line Trips
summary: Fire activity under transmission lines in the Central Coast/Hunter region caused tripping of the 2M (Munmorah-Tuggerah 132 kV) and 26 (Munmorah-Sydney West 330 kV) lines. This incident occurred during the 2019-2020 Black Summer bushfire crisis.
source: AEMO Power System Operating Incident Report - NSW Line Trips January 2020

timeline.event: Bushfire activity reported under transmission corridor near Munmorah
Munmorah-Tuggerah 2M line (132 kV) trips due to smoke ionisation
Network support constraints invoked for central coast region
Load at risk warnings issued for Central Coast area
2M line returned to service following fire containment
26 line returned to service, system restored

aemoNameMapping.notes: The 132 kV Munmorah-Tuggerah line is not in the GA transmission dataset (likely classified as sub-transmission). GA has both 'Munmorah' and 'Lake Munmorah' substations.

notes: This incident was part of the widespread bushfire impacts across NSW during the 2019-2020 Black Summer. The Central Coast region was particularly affected with multiple transmission contingencies.
